title.narrative: Start Network: Strengthening the resilience of local communities to crisis in Bangladesh

description.narrative: IMPACT: Humanitarian responses are localised, rapid, informed and adapted to the needs of the affected population.OUTCOME 1: Humanitarian action is timely, proactive, contextualised, coordinated, needs-driven, and informed by those closest to crises.OUTCOME 2: SFB member NGOs have organisational readiness and equal opportunities to access direct funding and influence decisions, thereby fostering a more locally-led, accountable humanitarian response.OUTCOME 3: Humanitarian action is locally informed and generating evidence to influence a more appropriate, effective and efficient humanitarian system.OUTPUT 1: SFB provides rapid funding to anticipated, under-funded, small to medium scale humanitarian crises.OUTPUT 2: SFB provides organisational strengthening support to LNNGO members for their readiness to access direct funding and quality implementation.OUTPUT 3: SFB influences the humanitarian system through innovative ways of working and evidence-based advocacy.

Start Fund Bangladesh (SFB), managed by Start Network, is a rapid-response humanitarian funding mechanism supported by Sida (Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency). The programme strengthens the resilience of local communities to crisis in Bangladesh by providing rapid, locally-led funding to under-funded humanitarian crises, building the organisational capacity of local and national NGO (LNNGO) members, and influencing the humanitarian system through evidence-based advocacy and innovative ways of working. The project period runs from January 2025 to December 2025.

description.narrative: Assumptions: Crises occur which are relevant for emergency response, in areas that are accessible by SFB members. Member agencies have capacity for rapid responses in emergencies. Delay FD6 approval from the government may have implications on timeliness of the response when regular alerts are raised. Limited control over the demand of the disbursement pot – fewer crises may lead to underutilisation of resources. Anticipatory action depends on meeting predefined thresholds and triggers specific to different hazards (assumption for indicator I1.1).
